correctness.rationale: Explicit shared-rate hypotheses, positivity and quantifiers are specified. Algebraically the hazard difference is a three-term exponential sum for three classes with at most one coefficient sign change by transitivity of the weight ratios; multiplication by the boundary exponential proves at most one real root. For the four-class witness, exact polynomial identities, positive quadratic discriminant test, Descartes rule and rational sign brackets prove strict all-time survival dominance and exactly two simple hazard crossover ages. CHECK.py verifies exact witness arithmetic but is not used to replace the analytic infinite proof.

The finding is specifically about crossing counts of the ratio-derived aggregate hazards with a shared set of rates, simultaneously with strict all-age survival order; a result about crossings of the survival densities alone does not automatically imply the hazard-rank conclusion.

originality.rationale: Relevant public primary frailty and mixture comparison sources were inspected to their accessible extent. The accessible 2014 full-text review has only a different single gamma-crossover comparison and general identities, while no exact sharp finite common-support threshold with strict survival dominance was found. The inaccessible original 1989 variation-diminishing paper presents a genuine residual risk; the status is provisional historical priority, not independent certification.

value.rationale: The minimal number of heterogeneous mortality risk classes necessary for double hazard-ranking reversal is a natural structural invariant in frailty demography. The sharp four-class witness simultaneously enforces strict survival dominance, demonstrating a substantive contrast between all-age survival and instantaneous hazards that cannot be inferred from either ordering alone. This is a complete self-contained theorem, not a numerical parameter slice or a request for future work.
